body:
# the contributor audit: orientation-separated moments and projective coarea


`candidate 5b3b585d1663ccd0`.
The universal common scalar interval-intersection assertion remains
unproved and is not an audited conclusion.

The layer mixture uses one orientation at a time and preserves the
actual cap mass, raw vertical coarea, and vertical section moment with
the same probability weights. Separate lower and upper moment
multipliers are therefore legitimate. The earlier certificate that
cancelled moments between opposite orientations does not test these
quantifiers. For a finite list, the scalar interval intersection and
the two independent moment multipliers are equivalent by explicit
upper/lower bounds. Extreme zero-moment mixtures have at most two
slopes; positive coareas justify the linear-fractional reduction.

For a common affine support ell=r0(1+b0 z)>=r(z)>0, the map
q=z/[s(1+b0 z)] is increasing on every actual section interval and has
image in [-r0,r0]. Its Jacobian and r<=ell give
integral (1+b0 z)^(-d) d sigma_s <=r0^(d-1).
The exponent cancellation uses d=m+1 exactly, including m=1.
The tangent inequality for the convex denominator then yields
C(s)-d b0 M(s)<=C(0) pointwise. Every same-orientation zero-M mixture
thus has coarea at most C(0). If b0 is nonzero, equality forces its
section measure to be at z=0; no uniform gap near slope zero follows.

The tail identity retains both full and empty axial tails. Consequently
the new coarea bound does not alone determine cap masses or prove the
common scalar intervals intersect. No continuous-profile result here
has yet been transferred to arbitrary mixed-integer fibers.

## Section 7: common deletion record, also PASS

the contributor subsequently read Section 7 in full. The tangent projective chart has a concave profile attaining its maximum at zero. Its section densities e_s(q) are pointwise nonincreasing in s, including finite-domain deletions. The inverse-chart Jacobian gives the printed coarea exponent d and moment exponent d+1. Denominators have a common positive lower bound on actual support. A positive C1 extension outside that range permits the bounded-variation product rule without using a pole outside support. The derivative of the weight is d b0 M/s; the remaining derivative is a nonpositive deletion measure. The exact identity P'=-M/s cancels the former term. Hence F=C+d b0(P-V/2) decreases to zero. The large-s limit uses the positive minimum of r on its original compact interval. This conclusion does not assert a sharp correlation between separately averaged C and F.

The proposed horizontal-tangent inverse-arm formulas were independently checked algebraically by the contributor and Rate. At fixed slope intersections, subtracting the zero-M equation from the cap objective cancels the two quadratic tail terms in all dimensions. This is an exact reduction, not yet a localization theorem or multiplier certificate.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
